div.head: VI Atr Lat 7
div.ab: K. Incantatores autem, magos, phithonicos et ueneficos necne idolorum cultores accriter oportet constringere uel etiam ex patria eicere.
div.note: Latin paraphrase of VI Atr (early 11th c.; K = Cotton Claudius A III f. 30, perhaps by Archbishop Wulfstan), text in column K (Liebermann’s text; until October 2026 in column T). Liebermann gives no German translation for it: for the meaning see the matching Old English chapter of VI Atr above, which it paraphrases (Liebermann prints in small type the words that correspond exactly to the Old English).; T: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Liebermann’s Latin Paraphrase)”, now “∅ (moved to K)”)

note.seg: Das Wort kommt bei Tertullian, diese Orthographie bei Ducange vor. Neben Götzendienst steht Zauber (s. d. Gl 1a) auch sonst
The word occurs in Tertullian, this spelling in Ducange. Sorcery (see that word in Gl 1a) appears alongside idolatry elsewhere too
scincræftiga belegt Toller nur hierher. Doch ist der Sinn gesichert durch scincræft, -gedwola, -hiw, -(ge)lac, -læca, -læce, -læc, -lic, -seoc
Toller cites scincræftiga only from this passage. The meaning is, however, assured by scincræft, -gedwola, -hiw, -(ge)lac, -læca, -læce, -læc, -lic, -seoc
Hinzuzudenken ist, dass der Zauber (s. d. Gl 3—4) einen Todesfall verursacht hatte; nur dann bedroht ihn Todesstrafe
It must be understood that the sorcery (see that word in Gl 3—4) had caused a death; only in that case is it threatened with the death penalty
